fine_lines.title: a taste of your own medicine vs get the short straw
words: a taste of your own medicine
fine_lines.explanation_ar: a taste of your own medicine = تتلقى نفس المعاملة السيئة التي كنت تعامل بها الآخرين (تستحقها). get/draw the short straw = تكون الشخص الذي يحصل على المهمة أو النتيجة الأسوأ في المجموعة (حظ سيئ).
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'A taste of your own medicine' = receiving the same bad treatment you gave others (you deserve it). 'Get (or draw) the short straw' = being the one in a group who gets the worst job or result (bad luck).

examples.word: a taste of your own medicine
examples.sentence: He always interrupts – today someone interrupted him. A taste of his own medicine!
I got the short straw and had to clean the bathroom.

fine_lines.title: throw shade vs hot under the collar
fine_lines.explanation_ar: throw shade (at someone) = تنتقد شخصاً أو تقلّل من شأنه بطريقة خفية أو علنية. hot under the collar = تصبح غاضباً أو منزعجاً جداً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Throw shade (at someone)' = criticise or disrespect someone, often in a quiet, clever way. 'Hot under the collar' = becoming very annoyed or angry.

examples.sentence: She threw shade at my shoes by saying 'Nice... for a museum'.
He gets hot under the collar when people are late.

fine_lines.title: wing it vs cough up
fine_lines.explanation_ar: wing it = تفعل شيئاً دون تحضير وترتجل. cough up = تدفع المال (غالباً وأنت لا تريد).
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Wing it' = do something without preparing, improvise. 'Cough up' = pay money, usually when you don't want to.

examples.sentence: I didn't study, so I'll have to wing it.
We had to cough up £20 for parking.

expressions.meaning_ar: يعيش في عزلة فكرية مع أشخاص يفكرون مثله ولا يتقبّل الأفكار المختلفة
expressions.meaning_en: to live only with people who think like you and not accept different ideas
expressions.example: He only reads news that agrees with him – he's living in a bubble.

expressions.meaning_en: the same bad treatment that you have given to others
expressions.example: She always laughs at others, so it was a taste of her own medicine when they laughed at her.

expressions.meaning_en: to have a lot of good luck at the same time
expressions.example: A new job and a new flat in one week – all my Christmases have come at once!

expressions.meaning_ar: عنده موهبة طبيعية في إيجاد شيء
expressions.meaning_en: to have a natural ability to find something

He got hot under the collar when the train was cancelled again.

expressions.meaning_ar: يحصل على المهمة أو النتيجة الأسوأ في المجموعة
expressions.meaning_en: to be the person in a group who gets the worst job or result
expressions.example: I drew the short straw – I'm working on the holiday.

expressions.meaning_ar: ينتقد شخصاً أو يقلّل من شأنه، غالباً بأسلوب خفي
expressions.meaning_en: to criticise or disrespect someone, often in a quiet or clever way
expressions.example: Was that comment about my cooking throwing shade?

expressions.meaning_ar: فريق أو شخص صغير يهزم منافساً أكبر وأقوى بكثير
expressions.meaning_en: a small team or person that beats a much bigger, stronger one
expressions.example: The village team were the giant killers of the cup this year.

expressions.meaning_en: to pay money, especially when you don't want to
expressions.example: I had to cough up £50 to fix my phone screen.

expressions.meaning_en: to do something without preparing; improvise
expressions.example: I forgot my notes, so I just winged it.

grammar.title: Phrasal verbs with an object: cough up
grammar.explanation_ar: cough up فعل مركّب يمكن أن يأخذ مفعولاً: cough up the money / cough the money up. لكن مع الضمير يجب أن يأتي في الوسط: cough it up (وليس cough up it).
grammar.explanation_en: 'Cough up' is a phrasal verb that can take an object: cough up the money / cough the money up. With a pronoun, it must go in the middle: cough it up (not 'cough up it').
